sections.history: Thiruvanpurushothamam stands among paddy fields in Thirunangur, about 10 km by road from Sirkazhi and from Thiruvenkadu, in Chola Nadu of the old Tamil country. It is one of the 108 Divya Desams sung by the Alvars in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham, and one of the eleven Thirunangur Tirupathis hymned by Thirumangai Alvar. The presiding Lord is Purushothama Perumal, with the Goddess Purushothama Nayaki, and both are worshipped standing. No inscription or royal patron is firmly recorded, so the shrine's age rests on the Alvar's hymns, placed between the seventh and ninth centuries.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian temple set among the green of the paddy fields, with a three-tiered vimana rising over the sanctum. The Lord and the Goddess both stand in the sanctum, Purushothama Perumal with Purushothama Nayaki. Its sacred tank, the Thiruparkadal Theertham, takes its name from Thiruparkadal, the ocean of milk, and so keeps the temple's central story before every visitor who stops at the water.
sections.legends: The sthala purana tells that the sage Vyaghrapada once left his young son Upamanyu in the temple while he went to gather flowers. The hungry child cried, and at the Goddess's request Purushothama Perumal brought milk from Thiruparkadal, the ocean of milk, and fed him. The tank is named for that milk. Upamanyu is remembered in tradition as a child whose hunger was answered by the Lord himself.
sections.festivals: The shrine joins the Garuda Sevai on the day after Thai Amavasai (January–February), when its utsavar is taken on a Garuda vahana to Thirumanimadam to meet the other lords of Thirunangur, and the Thirumangai Alvar Mangalasasana Utsavam recalls the hymns. Tradition holds that seeing all eleven together equals visiting each one.
sections.experience: Stop at the Thiruparkadal Theertham and recall the story of the child and the milk before entering. The setting is the quiet countryside of Thirunangur, a fine place for an unhurried visit; the shrine lies about 10 km by road from Sirkazhi and can be taken in with the other Tirupathis in a day.

visit.timings: Darshan is generally held in morning and evening sessions with a midday break; the Garuda Sevai day is by far the busiest. Confirm timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Thirunangur lies about 10 km by road south-east of Sirkazhi (Sirkali) in Mayiladuthurai district. Sirkazhi, on the Chennai–Mayiladuthurai railway line, is the nearest station, and Tiruchirappalli, about 160 km away, the nearest major airport. Auto-rickshaws and taxis from Sirkazhi reach the village; the eleven shrines lie among paddy fields close to one another.
